title: One Arrow, Two Parts: Vectors Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A ladder against a wall, a kite string, a ramp: each slanted line is secretly doing two jobs at once. Aarav cuts across the college ground on his bicycle at 5 m/s, and his friend asks how fast he is really going east, and how fast north. One slanted arrow holds both answers. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (NCERT Chapter 3, Motion in a Plane) we split any vector in a plane into its x and y components.

You will turn an arrow through a full circle on a live sim and watch Ax and Ay trace a cosine wave and a sine wave on the graph, with a slow-mo replay in the second quadrant. We derive Ax = A cos theta, Ay = A sin theta, the size from Pythagoras and the direction from tan theta, compare 30 and 60 degrees side by side, read the signs in all four quadrants and add vectors part by part, with two pause-and-think questions. Then a worked example with two bicycle rides, the exam trap of reading the angle from tan theta in the wrong quadrant, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.

In this video:

2:16 30 degrees vs 60 degrees + pause and think
2:47 Signs in the four quadrants + pause and think
3:20 Adding vectors part by part
3:32 Worked example: two bicycle rides
4:16 Exam trap: the angle from tan theta
4:43 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
